claims.claim: The Patents Law (Amendment No. 15) Bill, 5786-2025 was published as a government bill in Reshumot, Government Bills 1920, on 30 December 2025.

claims.claim: Section 16c proposed by the bill would let the applicant, or a person other than the applicant, demand examination of a patent application within four years of the Israeli filing date. The explanatory notes state that if the applicant does not demand examination within four years the application is refused and no patent is registered.

claims.claim: The bill proposes a new Israeli provisional patent application with relatively relaxed filing requirements, which expires as if it had never been filed after a year unless the applicant converts it into a regular application.

claims.claim: The bill would extend the grace period so that a publication made during the 12 months before the application date by the owner of the invention, by a predecessor in title, or by another person with their consent, is not treated as prior art defeating novelty or inventive step.

claims.claim: The bill would remove the time limit that currently applies to the submission of documents and references by a third party, and would allow the third party to attach explanations and relevant citations to that material.

claims.claim: Chapter Six of the Patents Law governs inventions of defence interest. Section 94 lets the Minister of Defense order the Registrar to refrain from acting on an application and restrict publication, and Section 98 bars an Israeli national or permanent resident from filing abroad an application for an invention that is weaponry, ammunition or otherwise of military value without prior written permission from the Minister of Defense.
